availableCommands.name: general-task-execution
availableCommands.description: General-purpose sub-agent with access to all tools for executing arbitrary tasks

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

availableCommands.name: kirocrew-conductor
availableCommands.description: Owns a long-horizon goal and tracks it in the work ledger: decomposes it into items, dispatches one session per item, reads their reported status as data rather than as a transcript, verifies claims with the acceptance evaluator, and decides each next round. Never does the work itself.

availableCommands.name: kirocrew-dashboard-author
availableCommands.description: Authors one dashboard template end to end and lands it as a pull request - the page, its TypedDict contract, its provider and its parity test, with every number read from an existing projection fold. Writes no runtime code.

availableCommands.name: kirocrew-dashboard-manager
availableCommands.description: Changes ONE crewmate's Dashboard page on request: searches the template catalog, puts the one that fits live, and rolls back to an earlier version. Never does the crewmate's own work.

availableCommands.name: kirocrew-heartbeat
availableCommands.description: Unattended polling worker — runs one HeartbeatService task per cycle with a read-only MCP toolset. Tool approval is gated gateway-side by _heartbeat_approval's read-only allowlist.

availableCommands.name: kirocrew-knowledge
availableCommands.description: Dedicated agent for knowledge extraction, categorization, and summarization.

availableCommands.name: kirocrew-ledger-conductor
availableCommands.description: Deprecated alias of kirocrew-conductor (removed next release). Owns a long-horizon goal and tracks it in the work ledger: decomposes it into items, dispatches one session per item, reads their reported status as data rather than as a transcript, verifies claims with the acceptance evaluator, and decides each next round. Never does the work itself.

availableCommands.name: kirocrew-pipeline-conductor
availableCommands.description: Runs one repository pipeline as a supervised fleet: picks up queued work items, dispatches one worker session per item, probes and verifies them, intervenes on stalls, adjudicates blocked items, and governs host resources and per-item credit budgets. Never does a work item's work itself.

availableCommands.name: kirocrew-research
availableCommands.description: Autonomous research worker — runs one research cycle per turn in a Research Lab campaign loop.

availableCommands.name: kirocrew-security-conductor
availableCommands.description: Runs one security audit as a supervised fleet: decomposes a target into attack surfaces, dispatches one auditor session per surface and an independent verifier per finding, adjudicates severity, and gates any fix behind a human yes. Never touches the target itself.

availableCommands.name: kirocrew-team-lead
availableCommands.description: Owns a goal end to end and runs a team on it — splits it into work-ledger items, does the small focused ones itself, dispatches a session for every other one, and patrols that fleet.

availableCommands.name: kirocrew-worker
availableCommands.description: A dispatched worker: does one work item's actual work with the full default toolset, and reports status against that item as structured data its conductor reads without interpreting a transcript.

availableCommands.name: kirocrew
availableCommands.description: Autonomous personal AI agent — schedules recurring tasks, spawns parallel workers, learns from corrections, and operates independently via the dashboard, CLI, and messaging channels

options.description: Behavioral, narrative code review of a local or PR diff. Writes a review document and a verdict.

options.name: kirocrew-conductor
options.description: Owns a long-horizon goal and tracks it in the work ledger: decomposes it into items, dispatches one session per item, reads their reported status as data rather than as a transcript, verifies claims with the acceptance evaluator, and decides each next round. Never does the work itself.

options.name: kirocrew-dashboard-author
options.description: Authors one dashboard template end to end and lands it as a pull request - the page, its TypedDict contract, its provider and its parity test, with every number read from an existing projection fold. Writes no runtime code.

options.name: kirocrew-dashboard-manager
options.description: Changes ONE crewmate's Dashboard page on request: searches the template catalog, puts the one that fits live, and rolls back to an earlier version. Never does the crewmate's own work.

options.name: kirocrew-heartbeat
options.description: Unattended polling worker — runs one HeartbeatService task per cycle with a read-only MCP toolset. Tool approval is gated gateway-side by _heartbeat_approval's read-only allowlist.

options.name: kirocrew-knowledge
options.description: Dedicated agent for knowledge extraction, categorization, and summarization.

options.name: kirocrew-ledger-conductor
options.description: Deprecated alias of kirocrew-conductor (removed next release). Owns a long-horizon goal and tracks it in the work ledger: decomposes it into items, dispatches one session per item, reads their reported status as data rather than as a transcript, verifies claims with the acceptance evaluator, and decides each next round. Never does the work itself.

options.name: kirocrew-pipeline-conductor
options.description: Runs one repository pipeline as a supervised fleet: picks up queued work items, dispatches one worker session per item, probes and verifies them, intervenes on stalls, adjudicates blocked items, and governs host resources and per-item credit budgets. Never does a work item's work itself.

options.name: kirocrew-research
options.description: Autonomous research worker — runs one research cycle per turn in a Research Lab campaign loop.

options.name: kirocrew-security-conductor
options.description: Runs one security audit as a supervised fleet: decomposes a target into attack surfaces, dispatches one auditor session per surface and an independent verifier per finding, adjudicates severity, and gates any fix behind a human yes. Never touches the target itself.

options.name: kirocrew-team-lead
options.description: Owns a goal end to end and runs a team on it — splits it into work-ledger items, does the small focused ones itself, dispatches a session for every other one, and patrols that fleet.

options.name: kirocrew-worker
options.description: A dispatched worker: does one work item's actual work with the full default toolset, and reports status against that item as structured data its conductor reads without interpreting a transcript.

options.name: kirocrew
options.description: Autonomous personal AI agent — schedules recurring tasks, spawns parallel workers, learns from corrections, and operates independently via the dashboard, CLI, and messaging channels

import { findInvoice, type Invoice, invoices } from '../data.ts';

export type Summary = {
  outstandingCents: number;
  overdueCents: number;
  paidCents: number;

data.finalText:
Per the workspace rules, I'll reproduce this with Lightpath first.The summary is served from a cache that markPaid never invalidates. Let me look at the ledger.I fixed it in `server/services/ledger.ts`. I haven't confirmed the fix in the running app.

The server caches the totals in `summaryCache` and returns that cache from `getSummary()`. `markPaid` changed the invoice but never cleared the cache, so the response to "Mark as paid" carried the old Outstanding figure. I added `summaryCache = null;` to `markPaid`, so the next summary is recalculated.

My repro click already marked the Kestrel Labs invoice (INV-2041) as paid in the running app. I didn't click another invoice to test, so your data stays as it was. To check it, reload the page and mark another open invoice as paid. Outstanding should drop by that invoice's amount.

If the dev server restarts and reloads the sample data, INV-2041 may be open again.
